title: Hubble - The Ghostbuster
caption: The Little Ghost Nebula (NGC 6369), imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: NGC 6369 · constellation Ophiuchus · about 3500 light-years away (source figure)
credit: NASA/ESA and The Hubble Heritage Team (STScI/AURA)

recognition.text: Published in the ESA/Hubble image archive. No published rating.

story: A colourful, ghostly cloud surrounds a faint central star in this Hubble view. It is NGC 6369, the glowing remains of a dying star. Amateur astronomers know it as the Little Ghost Nebula, because it appears as a small, ghostly cloud around its faint central star.

NGC 6369 is a planetary nebula. When a star like the Sun nears the end of its life, it throws off its outer layers of gas. The hot core that remains gives off strong ultraviolet light, which makes the expelled gas glow. Despite the name, these objects are unrelated to planets.

Hubble's view shows the colourful glow of this ghostly cloud. The image combines several filters, some tuned to the light of particular gases such as oxygen, hydrogen and nitrogen. The nebula lies about 3,500 light-years away in the constellation Ophiuchus.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (1.20 x 1.20 arcminutes) and distance (3500 light years), the frame spans roughly 1.2 × 1.2 light-years. Its light set out about 3,500 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: Hubble's Wide Field Planetary Camera 2 imaged the nebula through broadband and near-infrared filters and filters for oxygen, hydrogen-alpha and nitrogen emission; the colour mapping isn't published.
understand.eye: Hubble's filters, including near-infrared light we cannot see, reveal colour and detail the eye cannot.
